text:
Marathon Petroleum bounced back 1.08% today, recovering some ground after a sharp 4.6% drop yesterday (October 27th). The recovery came as oil prices rose on geopolitical concerns—the U.S. reportedly preparing for strikes against Iran, which typically supports crude prices. However, the broader refining picture remains a headwind: refining margins (the profit refiners make turning crude into gasoline and diesel) are shrinking, and gasoline and diesel inventories remain elevated, both of which compress the margins refiners earn on each barrel processed.

The two-week decline of 9.12% reflects this margin squeeze eating into profits faster than higher oil prices can offset. While refineries are running hard at 92.8% capacity, they're competing against rising global fuel supply and inventory levels that leave less room to mark up products. The report about potential Russian diesel entering the market adds another layer of supply pressure, even if volumes are expected to be small.
